name: Grid-following inverter
summary: An inverter that tracks an existing network voltage with a phase-locked loop and injects controlled current into it.
description: A grid-following inverter measures the network voltage, locks to it with a phase-locked loop and injects a controlled current. Most rooftop and utility-scale solar inverters work this way. They need a stable voltage from the grid, a synchronous machine or a grid-forming inverter to operate, and they disconnect when that reference is lost.

Drawings use the standard inverter symbol with a GFL note or a current-source annotation. Anti-islanding protection, often shown as a protection relay or a function list, is associated with this type so that it does not energise a dead network.

In weak networks with high converter penetration, grid-following control can become unstable, so system strength studies are needed. The symbol does not show the phase-locked loop settings or the reactive power mode.
readingNotes: Check that a forming source exists if the inverter is expected to run in an island.
Anti-islanding settings are often listed as protection functions next to the inverter.
drawingChecklist: State reactive power mode and ride-through settings.
distinction: A grid-following inverter needs an external voltage reference; a grid-forming inverter provides that reference.
